root_cause.text: The mvpp2 XDP receive path in `mvpp2_rx()` initialized every `xdp_buff` with `PAGE_SIZE` instead of the actual BM pool buffer size (`bm_pool->frag_size`), so XDP helpers could treat short RX buffers as having more tailroom than they really did.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `xdp_init_buff(&xdp, PAGE_SIZE, xdp_rxq);` to `xdp_init_buff(&xdp, bm_pool->frag_size, xdp_rxq);`, and the CVE text says short pool buffers can be smaller than `PAGE_SIZE`, making `bpf_xdp_adjust_tail()` able to grow packets past the real allocation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the buffer pool fragment size when initializing XDP buffers to match the actual RX buffer layout.
intent_record.what: In mvpp2_rx(), the call to xdp_init_buff() was changed to pass bm_pool->frag_size instead of PAGE_SIZE as the buffer size argument.
intent_record.how: This makes XDP buffer initialization use the actual fragment size of the backing buffer pool rather than a fixed page size, aligning XDP metadata with the real receive buffer capacity and avoiding size mismatches for non-page-sized fragments.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is not present in this version. The bug root cause was that XDP buffers were initialized with the wrong size, specifically using `PAGE_SIZE` instead of the BM pool buffer size (`bm_pool->frag_size`). In this diff, the old direct assignments `xdp.frame_sz = PAGE_SIZE;` and `xdp.rxq = ...` are removed, and initialization is moved to `xdp_init_buff(&xdp, PAGE_SIZE, xdp_rxq);`. Since the shown code no longer contains the original buggy manual setup in `mvpp2_rx()`, and it has been converted to the new helper-based initialization, the vulnerable construct is absent here. However, the snippet alone does not show whether the helper is passed the correct buffer size for this driver, so this specific function body is not enough to prove the underlying bug is fully fixed; still, the explicit old bug pattern is no longer present in the shown code.
